skill.name: design-dna
skill.description: Extract design tokens, qualitative style, and visual effects from references, then apply the resulting Design DNA profile to new content and interfaces.
skill.summary: Turn reference designs into reusable specifications and generated interfaces.
skill.author: zanwei

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, translated UTF-8 documentation, installation URLs, and references to screenshots. Three unpinned CDN examples create supply-chain exposure, while instructions to retrieve user-provided URLs create a separate SSRF and untrusted-content risk.

remediation.issue: Generated examples load latest library versions from a public CDN.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact library versions and add Subresource Integrity where supported, or bundle reviewed dependencies locally.

remediation.issue: The skill instructs agents to fetch arbitrary user-provided URLs and source assets.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict retrieval to HTTP and HTTPS, block private and local addresses, require confirmation, and treat fetched content as untrusted.

content.user_title: Extract and Apply Reusable Design DNA
content.value_statement: Teams struggle to convert visual references into precise, reusable design specifications. This skill extracts structured Design DNA and applies it to new content.
actual_capabilities: Presents a three-dimension schema covering design systems, qualitative style, and visual effects.
Analyzes images, screenshots, code, and URLs into a complete Design DNA profile.
Extracts colors, typography, spacing, layout, shape, elevation, motion, and component patterns.
Describes Canvas, WebGL, 3D, particle, shader, scroll, cursor, and SVG effects.
Generates self-contained HTML, CSS, and JavaScript from Design DNA and supplied content.
Applies accessibility, reduced-motion, responsive sizing, and rendering fallback checks.
limitations: Values inferred from screenshots are estimates and may not match original source tokens.
URL analysis requires network access and appropriate safeguards for untrusted destinations.
Heavy effects may require external libraries and capable graphics hardware.
Generated interfaces still require browser testing, accessibility review, and product validation.

use_cases.title: Document a Product Design System
use_cases.description: Convert approved screens into reusable tokens, style guidance, component patterns, and effect specifications.

use_cases.title: Rebuild a Visual Direction
use_cases.description: Analyze references and apply their visual language to new content without copying the original structure.

use_cases.title: Standardize Creative Prototypes
use_cases.description: Create a shared Design DNA profile that keeps agent-generated prototypes visually consistent across projects.

prompt_templates.title: Show the Design DNA Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the complete Design DNA schema. Explain the design system, design style, and visual effects dimensions in simple terms.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the available structure before starting an analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze One Reference
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this screenshot into a complete Design DNA profile. Separate observed values from estimates and note any uncertain effects.
prompt_templates.scenario: Extract a reusable specification from a single visual reference.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Several References
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these references into one Design DNA profile. Identify dominant patterns, record meaningful variants, and explain how conflicts were resolved.
prompt_templates.scenario: Synthesize a coherent direction from several sources.

prompt_templates.title: Generate and Validate an Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply this Design DNA profile to the supplied content. Build a responsive interface, implement specified effects, and verify accessibility, performance, and fallbacks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Produce a complete implementation from an approved specification.

output_examples.input: Analyze a screenshot of a compact analytics dashboard.
output: A restrained neutral palette with one high-contrast action color.
A dense twelve-column layout with compact spacing and small radii.
Minimal motion limited to chart transitions and focus feedback.

output_examples.input: Apply an approved Design DNA profile to product launch content.
output_examples.output: A responsive page using the specified tokens, composition, components, visual effects, reduced-motion behavior, and lightweight fallbacks.

output_examples.input: Compare three references that use different motion styles.
output_examples.output: A combined profile that identifies the dominant interaction pattern, preserves useful variants, and flags conflicting timing and intensity choices.

best_practices: Use clear, high-resolution references and include interaction recordings when motion matters.
Review inferred values and resolve uncertain fields before generating an implementation.
Pin external dependencies and test accessibility, performance, responsiveness, and reduced-motion behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not treat screenshot measurements as exact source values without verification.
Do not combine conflicting references without documenting dominant patterns and variants.
Do not enable heavy effects without fallbacks, cleanup, and performance testing.

faq.question: What is Design DNA?
faq.answer: It is a structured profile of measurable tokens, qualitative design choices, and special visual effects.

faq.question: Can it analyze screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It estimates visible properties from screenshots and should label values that cannot be verified.

faq.question: Can it analyze live websites?
faq.answer: Yes, when the agent has network access. Only trusted public URLs should be retrieved.

faq.question: What output does generation produce?
faq.answer: The default is self-contained HTML with inline CSS and JavaScript, unless you request a framework.

faq.question: Does it support advanced visual effects?
faq.answer: Yes. The schema covers Canvas, WebGL, 3D, particles, shaders, scroll effects, cursor effects, and SVG animation.

faq.question: Does the output require review?
faq.answer: Yes. Validate inferred tokens, licensing, accessibility, browser behavior, dependency integrity, and performance before production use.
